title: Two letters that ask you to stop and listen.
subtitle: Letters that open the surah and ask for attention
then: This surah came in Makkah in the year the Prophet ﷺ called the year of sorrow. A long boycott had just ended, and he had lost Abu Talib and Khadijah. It opens with two letters, Ha Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What they do for the listener is clear: stop, and listen to what follows.
now: You open the app between two notifications. Your thumb is already looking for the next thing. Two letters sit there that you cannot decode or rush. {idea}They slow you down on purpose.{/idea} The next lines are worth a full breath.
old: If I cannot understand a word, I can skip past it.
new: Some words are there to make me pause before I read on.
try: Before you read the next verse, put your phone on silent and take one slow breath.

title: The message comes from someone mighty and wise.
subtitle: Who sent the Book, and what that changes
then: The people of Makkah treated the Quran as one man's words. Ibn Kathir explains that the verse names its true source: {idea}Allah, of unimaginable glory, wise in what He says and does.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ was being pushed hard, but the message was not his to lose.
now: You get a letter from a hospital, a bank, a school. You read it differently depending on who signed it. A note from a friend you skim. {reward}A note from someone who knows everything and means well,{/reward} you read twice.
old: This is an old book that people quote at me.
new: This is a message from the One who is both strong and wise, sent to me.
try: Read one verse today as if it had your name on the envelope.

title: Nothing was made as a game, and everything has an end date.
subtitle: Creation has a purpose and a fixed term
then: Ibn Kathir says the heavens and earth were made {idea}not in idle play and falsehood{/idea}, and for a duration that will not grow or shrink. The disbelievers of Makkah had a Book and a Messenger ﷺ in front of them. {trap}They were distracted and kept turning away.{/trap}
now: Some nights the world feels like noise: news, scrolling, bills, the same week again. It is easy to think none of it adds up. {idea}This verse says it does, and it has a deadline.{/idea} The clock on your life is real, not random.
old: Life just happens, and it will keep going like this.
new: The world was made with purpose, and it has a set time to end.
try: Look at the sky for one minute tonight and ask what it was made for.

title: Show me what they made, or show me your proof.
subtitle: A fair challenge to anything worshipped besides Allah
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask the idol worshippers simple questions. {idea}What have your idols made? Bring a book or a trace of knowledge.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes they did not own even the thin skin on a date stone. {trap}They had no proof from revelation or from reason.{/trap}
now: You give hours to something because everyone around you does. The trend, the habit, the thing you check first each morning. Ask it the verse's question. {idea}What has it actually made in my life? Where is the proof?{/idea}
old: Lots of people rely on it, so it must be worth it.
new: Before I trust something, I can ask what it has made and what proof it has.
try: Pick one habit you lean on. Write one honest line on what it has given you.

title: Calling out to something that cannot hear you.
subtitle: The most lost person, in one picture
then: Ibn Kathir says no one is more misguided than a person who asks idols for what they cannot give. {trap}They are senseless stones. They do not even know they are being asked.{/trap} The caller waits for an answer that will not come.
now: You keep refreshing for a reply from someone who will never write back. You keep hoping a purchase will make you feel safe. {trap}The call goes out, nothing comes back.{/trap} {idea}Allah is the One who hears.{/idea}
old: If I keep asking, it will eventually come through for me.
new: Only Allah hears every call, so my real asking belongs with Him.
try: Take one worry you have been carrying alone and say it to Allah in your own words.

title: What you leaned on will turn against you.
subtitle: False supports desert you when you need them most
then: On the Day of gathering, the things people worshipped will become their enemies and deny they were ever worshipped. Ibn Kathir links it to Ibrahim's words: {trap}the love they shared in this life turns to cursing each other.{/trap} They betray them when they need them most.
now: The friend group you bent your values to fit. The boss you pleased by cutting corners. When it goes wrong, they say they never asked you to. {trap}What you leaned on steps back.{/trap} {idea}Lean only on what will stand with you later.{/idea}
old: The people and things I go along with will back me up.
new: Anything I put in Allah's place will step away from me at the moment I need it.
try: Notice one choice you make just to keep someone pleased. Ask if it pleases Allah too.

title: Calling clear truth magic so you do not have to face it.
subtitle: A label used to avoid what was clear
then: When the clear verses were recited, the leaders of Makkah said {trap}this is plain magic.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says in this they lied and went astray. {idea}The verse calls it what it was: the truth that had come to them.{/idea}
now: Someone you love points out a thing you need to change. Instead of thinking about it, you say they are just being dramatic. {trap}A quick label closes the door.{/trap} {idea}The truth was still in the room.{/idea}
old: If I can name it as something silly, I do not have to deal with it.
new: Putting a label on the truth does not make it any less true.
try: Think of one piece of advice you brushed off. Give it two honest minutes today.

title: If he made it up, who could protect him?
subtitle: The answer of the Prophet ﷺ to the charge of invention
then: They said Muhammad ﷺ forged the Quran. He answers: {idea}if I lied about Allah, none of you could protect me from Him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the verse is a serious warning, yet it closes with {reward}the Forgiving, the Merciful{/reward}, an invitation to turn back.
now: You have said harsh things about someone, maybe in a group chat. Then you hear they were honest all along. The verse shows a hard truth and a soft one together. {reward}The door to turn back is still open.{/reward}
old: Once I have taken a side, I cannot go back on it.
new: Even after I have been wrong out loud, Allah keeps forgiveness open.
try: If you spoke unfairly about someone, quietly correct it with one person today.

title: Not something new, and not claiming to know the unseen.
subtitle: The humility of the Prophet ﷺ about what he knew

row.title: I do not know
sub: what will be done with us

then: Ibn Kathir records that when Uthman bin Maz'un died, a woman said Allah had surely honored him. The Prophet ﷺ asked how she knew, and said {idea}even he did not know what would happen to him{/idea}, though he hoped good for Uthman. {reward}Later she dreamed of Uthman with a flowing spring, and the Prophet ﷺ said it was his deeds.{/reward}
now: At a funeral, someone says he is definitely in Paradise. Online, someone says another person is definitely lost. {trap}Both speak as if they can see the unseen.{/trap} {idea}Hope for people, pray for them, and leave the verdict to Allah.{/idea}
old: I can tell who is good and who is lost.
new: Even the Prophet ﷺ only hoped, so I can hope and pray and leave the judgment to Allah.
try: Make a short prayer today for someone who passed away, without deciding their fate.

title: Someone who knew the earlier books believed, while you refused.
subtitle: A witness from those with scripture
then: Ibn Kathir says the earlier scriptures foretold things like what the Quran brings. {reward}A person from the Children of Israel recognized it and believed.{/reward} Many early scholars said this includes Abdullah bin Salam. {trap}The Makkan leaders, with no such knowledge, refused out of pride.{/trap}
now: A new colleague with real experience says the plan is sound. You, with less experience, keep fighting it because it was not your idea. {trap}Pride makes you argue past the expert.{/trap} {idea}Notice who recognizes the truth, and why.{/idea}
old: If I did not think of it first, I do not have to accept it.
new: When people who know the subject recognize the truth, my pride should not be the one deciding.
try: Ask one person who knows more than you for their view on something, and just listen.

title: If it were good, the poor would not have got there first.
subtitle: Judging truth by who follows it
then: The leaders of Makkah said {trap}if this were any good, those people would not have beaten us to it.{/trap} They meant Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and servants. Ibn Kathir says they thought their status made them special to Allah. When they did not take guidance, they called it an ancient lie.
now: You hear about a good idea, then see who is sharing it: the quiet kid, the cleaner, the new person. Something in you dismisses it. {trap}That is judging the message by the messenger's rank.{/trap} {idea}Good is good, whoever got there first.{/idea}
old: If people of no status are into it, it is probably not worth much.
new: Truth is not ranked by the status of the people who accept it.
try: Listen fully today to someone you usually overlook, and thank them.

title: Not an old lie, but the same light that came to Musa.
subtitle: The Quran confirms what came before it
then: They had called the Quran {trap}an ancient falsehood.{/trap} The verse answers: before it came the Book of Musa, a guide and a mercy, and this Book confirms it in clear Arabic. Ibn Kathir says it carries {trap}a warning to wrongdoers{/trap} and {reward}glad tidings to the believers.{/reward}
now: Your grandmother's advice sounds old until your own child is born and you hear yourself repeating it. {idea}Old does not mean false. Sometimes old means proven.{/idea} The same guidance kept coming because people kept needing it.
old: It is old, so it does not speak to my life now.
new: The same guidance has come again and again because people have always needed it.
try: Ask an older relative for one piece of advice that has never let them down.

title: Say it once, then keep walking straight.
subtitle: Faith that is said and then stood on
then: The verse comes right after the warning to wrongdoers and good news to the doers of good. It describes those who say {idea}our Lord is Allah{/idea} and then stay on that course. Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}no fear about what is ahead, no grief over what they left behind.{/reward}
now: You felt it strongly in Ramadan. The prayers were on time, the phone was down. Then the ordinary weeks came back. {idea}This verse praises the staying, not just the starting.{/idea} Small and steady still counts as standing firm.
old: My faith only counts when I feel it strongly.
new: What counts is saying it and then quietly staying on the path day after day.
try: Choose one small act of worship you can keep every day this week, and start today.

title: A home that lasts, for what they kept doing.
subtitle: Paradise as the reward of a steady life
then: Those who said our Lord is Allah and stood firm are called {reward}the companions of Paradise, forever.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes the phrase for what they used to do: {idea}their deeds are a cause for reaching mercy and being surrounded by it.{/idea}
now: You keep a habit you cannot see paying off: a monthly charity transfer, a call to your mother every Sunday. It feels small. {idea}The verse says used to do: the repeated things.{/idea} {reward}Mercy meets what you kept doing.{/reward}
old: My small, repeated good deeds do not really add up to anything.
new: What I keep doing becomes a door for Allah's mercy.
try: Pick one good thing you already do regularly and do it today with intention.

title: Thirty months of her hardship, and a prayer at forty.
subtitle: Gratitude to parents and turning back at maturity
then: Right after speaking of faith, the verse turns to parents, as the Quran often does. Ibn Kathir describes {trap}the fatigue, sickness, heaviness and pain{/trap} a mother bears, and the thirty months of carrying and nursing. At forty, a person's mind and patience mature. {idea}Ibn Kathir says this is a call for anyone reaching forty to renew repentance.{/idea}
now: Your mother's text says she has not heard from you in a while. You are busy, a deadline, a meeting. Thirty months of your life she carried and fed you before you could say thanks. {reward}The prayer here thanks Allah for her too.{/reward} And it asks good for your own children.
old: My parents did what parents do. I will thank them when life slows down.
new: My parents' hardship is a gift I owe thanks for, to them and to Allah, now.
try: Call or message one of your parents today just to thank them for one specific thing.

title: Their best is accepted, their worst is overlooked.
subtitle: The promise for those who turn back

picture.label: What Allah does with their record

then: This is for the person in the verse before: grateful, praying for parents and children, turning back to Allah. Ibn Kathir says {reward}many of their errors will be forgiven and a modest amount of deeds will be accepted.{/reward} {idea}It is a promise of truth.{/idea}
now: You replay your worst moments at 2am: the shouting, the lie, the wasted years. You feel your good is too small to matter. {reward}This verse describes a Lord who takes the best and overlooks the rest{/reward} for those who turn back.
old: My mistakes outweigh anything good I have done.
new: When I turn back, Allah keeps my best and overlooks my worst.
try: Say one sincere sentence of repentance tonight, then name one good thing you did today.

title: Uff to his parents, while they pray for him.
subtitle: The other kind of child, and his parents' pleading
then: After the grateful child comes the opposite. Ibn Kathir says this is a general description of anyone who speaks to parents with contempt and denies resurrection. He notes the claim it was about Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Bakr is weak, and Aishah rejected it. {reward}The parents keep asking Allah to guide him.{/reward}
now: Your mother reminds you to pray and you roll your eyes, sigh, say not now. {trap}Uff is that sigh.{/trap} {reward}Meanwhile she is making dua for you every night.{/reward} Even when you disagree, the tone is the deed.
old: A sigh or an eye roll at my parents is not a big deal.
new: My tone to my parents matters, and their worried prayers for me deserve gentleness.
try: The next time a parent nags you today, answer with one soft sentence instead of a sigh.

title: Joining the line of those who lost before.
subtitle: Where that attitude ends up
then: Ibn Kathir says the word those confirms the previous verse describes a type of person, not one man. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said it is {trap}the disbelieving, sinful one who is undutiful to his parents and denies resurrection.{/trap} Such people end up with their likes from earlier generations.
now: It is easy to read this and think of someone else's rude son. {idea}The verse describes a pattern, so it is a mirror.{/idea} Contempt at home and dismissing the Hereafter tend to travel together. {reward}The pattern can be broken today.{/reward}
old: This is about some bad person from long ago.
new: This describes a pattern, and I can check myself for any piece of it.
try: Ask yourself honestly how you spoke to your parents this week. Fix one thing.

title: Everyone gets their exact level, and no one is wronged.
subtitle: Degrees for both sides, perfect fairness
then: After the grateful child and the scornful one, the verse says all have degrees. Ibn Kathir quotes Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd: {idea}the levels of the Fire descend, and those of Paradise ascend.{/idea} {reward}Allah will not wrong anyone, even by a speck of dust.{/reward}
now: At work, the person who does the least gets the same bonus as you. It stings. {idea}Here nothing is averaged out.{/idea} {reward}Every kind word to your parents, every hidden effort, gets its exact weight.{/reward}
old: What I do does not really change much in the end.
new: Every deed shifts my level, and none of it is lost or unfairly counted.
try: Do one good thing today that nobody will see, knowing it is counted exactly.

title: You spent all your good things in the world.
subtitle: Pleasure used up, arrogance answered
then: On the Day the disbelievers face the Fire, they are told they used up their good things in this life. Ibn Kathir says Umar bin Al-Khattab {idea}gave up many joys of food and drink, afraid of being like those reproached here.{/idea} {trap}Their arrogance and rebellion are answered with humiliation.{/trap}
now: Payday comes and the cart fills fast: food delivery, a new gadget, the upgrade. {idea}None of it is wrong in itself.{/idea} But if every good thing is spent on the now, with no thanks and no giving, {trap}the verse says something is being used up.{/trap}
old: I worked for it, so I should enjoy all of it right now.
new: Blessings are for thanks and sharing, not only for using up.
try: Skip one small treat today and give its price to someone in need.

title: Remember the brother of Aad, warning his own people.
subtitle: Hud among the sand dunes
then: Ibn Kathir says this story was told {reward}to console the Prophet ﷺ{/reward} as his people rejected him. Hud was sent to Aad at al-Ahqaf, a land of sand dunes; Qatadah said in Yemen. The surah takes its name from here. {idea}Other warners had come before and after him.{/idea}
now: You are the only one in the family who prays, or who speaks up at work about something wrong. It feels lonely. {reward}The verse says: remember those who stood where you stand.{/reward} Hud was a brother to his people, not a stranger shouting at them.
old: Nobody has ever been as alone as I am in this.
new: Others stood in the same spot before me, and their stories are told to steady me.
try: Read one short story of a Prophet today and notice what he faced.

title: Bring it on, if you are telling the truth.
subtitle: Daring the warning to come

row.title: bring it
sub: the threat, if it is real

then: Aad accused Hud of trying to pull them from their gods. Then they said {trap}bring us what you threaten us with.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they asked to hurry the punishment because they believed it would not happen.
now: The doctor says cut down on sugar or there will be trouble. You laugh and order dessert: show me. {trap}Daring a warning feels brave in the moment.{/trap} {idea}It usually just means you do not believe it yet.{/idea}
old: If it were really coming, it would have happened already.
new: Daring a warning is not courage; it is not believing it.
try: Think of one warning you have been laughing off. Take one small step toward it today.

title: When it comes is with Allah; my job is to tell you.
subtitle: Hud knows his role and its limits
then: Hud did not take the bait. Ibn Kathir paraphrases: {idea}Allah knows best about you; my duty is to deliver my message.{/idea} {trap}He told them plainly they were a people with no understanding.{/trap}
now: You advised your brother about a bad deal. He says, so when will it fail then? You cannot answer that. {idea}You can only say what you believe is true, kindly, and leave the outcome.{/idea}
old: If I give advice, I have to be able to prove exactly how it plays out.
new: My part is to say the truth clearly; the timing and results belong to Allah.
try: Give one honest piece of advice today and let go of needing to win the argument.

title: They saw a cloud and thought it was rain.
subtitle: What they cheered was what they had asked for

key.label: The habit of the Prophet ﷺ

then: Aad were in a drought, so a dark cloud made them glad. {trap}It was the wind they had asked to hurry.{/trap} Aishah said that when the Prophet ﷺ saw clouds or wind, worry showed on his face. {idea}He asked Allah for its good and sought refuge from its harm, and was relieved when rain fell.{/idea}
now: A big offer lands in your inbox. Everyone says it is perfect. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ would greet even welcome things with a prayer.{/idea} Not fear, just humility: you cannot always see what a cloud carries.
old: Anything that looks good coming my way must be good.
new: I can welcome what comes with a prayer for its good and protection from its harm.
try: Next time it rains or the wind picks up, ask Allah for its good and refuge from its harm.

title: Only their empty houses were left standing.
subtitle: The end of Aad, by their Lord's command
then: The wind destroyed everything it was permitted to destroy. Ibn Kathir says {trap}all of them were destroyed, and none were spared.{/trap} Only their homes remained. {idea}This is Allah's way with those who reject His Messengers and disobey Him.{/idea}
now: You drive past a grand old building, now empty, windows boarded. Someone once thought it would hold their name forever. {idea}Walls outlast people, but they do not carry anyone.{/idea} What you build inside yourself is what goes with you.
old: What I build in this world will keep me safe.
new: Buildings can outlast their owners, so my real safety is in how I live before Allah.
try: Next time you pass an old building, think of who built it and what they took with them.

title: They had eyes, ears and hearts, and used none of them.
subtitle: Strength and senses did not save them
then: Ibn Kathir says earlier nations had wealth and children far beyond what the Makkans had. They also had hearing, sight and hearts. {trap}None of it helped, because they used them to deny Allah's signs.{/trap} {idea}The listeners are told to beware of becoming like them.{/idea}
now: You are clever. You can out-argue anyone at dinner. You have a degree, a good salary, a sharp eye. {trap}All of that can be used to avoid the one question that matters.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks what your senses are actually for.{/idea}
old: Being smart and capable keeps me from being misled.
new: Intelligence only helps if I use it to see the truth, not to dodge it.
try: Use your eyes for one sign today: look closely at something living and thank Allah for it.

title: The ruins around you are a message told many ways.
subtitle: Destroyed towns the Makkans passed on trade routes
then: Ibn Kathir lists the towns near Makkah: {trap}Aad, Thamud, Saba, Madyan, and the people of Lut{/trap}, whose places the Makkans passed on their journeys. Allah explained the signs in different ways. {idea}The goal was that perhaps they would return.{/idea}
now: A cousin's divorce. A friend's health scare. A coworker who burned out. You hear these stories every month. {idea}Each one is a quiet sign, explained a different way, so you might turn back sooner.{/idea}
old: Other people's hard lessons are just their stories.
new: The lessons around me are signs repeated in many forms so that I might turn back.
try: Think of one hard thing that happened to someone you know. Write down what it teaches you.

title: Their go-betweens vanished when needed most.
subtitle: What they used to approach Allah left them
then: They claimed these gods were a means of getting closer to Allah. {trap}When the punishment came, the gods did not help; they were simply gone.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says it was their lie, and {trap}they failed in their reliance on them.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself you will get close to Allah once a certain person, a certain mood, a certain trip makes it easier. {idea}You do not need a go-between.{/idea} You can pray right now, from where you are sitting.
old: I need something or someone in between before I can reach Allah.
new: Nothing I invent can bring me near; Allah is reached directly.
try: Make one dua today with no plan and no middle step, just you and Allah.

title: Strangers stopped, hushed each other, and listened.
subtitle: The jinn at Nakhlah hearing the Quran
then: The surah introduction places this on the return from Ta'if, a hard time. Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ was reciting in prayer at Nakhlah. {idea}A group of jinn stopped, told each other to listen quietly, and heard it through.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said he did not see them. {reward}They went back to warn their own people.{/reward}
now: A recitation plays from a car, a shop, a phone near you. Most people keep talking. {idea}Someone who truly hears says hush, listen.{/idea} Then they carry what they heard home, to a sibling, a child, a friend.
old: When the Quran is playing, I can half-listen while I do other things.
new: The Quran deserves my silence, and what I hear in it is meant to be carried home.
try: Next time you hear the Quran today, stop what you are doing and listen until it ends.

title: We heard a Book after Musa that guides to truth.
subtitle: How the jinn summed up what they heard

row.title: guides
sub: to truth and a straight path

then: Back home, the jinn told their people they had heard a Book sent after Musa. Ibn Kathir notes they named Musa because the Tawrah was the main law before. {idea}It guides to truth in belief and to a straight path in deeds.{/idea} Its information is true and its commands are just.
now: A friend asks what the Quran is really about. You fumble. {idea}The jinn did it in one breath: it confirms what came before, it tells the truth, and it shows the way.{/idea} You can say that too, plainly.
old: I could never explain my faith simply to someone.
new: I can describe the Quran in a few honest words: true in what it says, just in what it asks.
try: Write a two-sentence answer to the question what is the Quran about, in your own words.

title: Answer the caller, and be forgiven and protected.
subtitle: The jinn invite their people
then: The jinn who had just listened now spoke as warners to their own. {idea}Respond to Allah's caller and believe in him.{/idea} {reward}Allah will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.{/reward}
now: You want your brother to come back to prayer. You could list what he does wrong. {reward}Or you could start with how much Allah wants to forgive.{/reward} The jinn, new to faith themselves, led with that.
old: To bring someone back, I need to show them how wrong they are.
new: An invitation can start with forgiveness and safety, not with blame.
try: Share one verse about Allah's forgiveness with someone who might need it today.

title: Ignoring the call does not get you away from Allah.
subtitle: No escape and no protector besides Him
then: The jinn finished their warning plainly. {trap}Whoever does not answer cannot escape on earth and has no protector besides Allah.{/trap} {idea}Such people are in clear error.{/idea}
now: You mute the reminder, change the subject, move to a new city, get very busy. {trap}None of that changes who you answer to.{/trap} {idea}Since you cannot run from Him, the safest place is turning to Him.{/idea}
old: If I stay busy and do not think about it, I am fine.
new: No distance or distraction takes me out of Allah's reach, so I can turn to Him now.
try: Find one reminder you have been snoozing and answer it today, even in a small way.

title: Making the skies did not tire Him; raising the dead will not.
subtitle: Creation as proof of resurrection

row.title: the sky was bigger
sub: He said be, and it was

then: This is said to those who doubted bodies would be raised. Ibn Kathir explains Allah commanded the heavens and earth be, {idea}and they were, with no refusal and no delay. Creating them did not tire Him.{/idea} So bringing the dead back is within His power.
now: You stand at a grave and the mind says: this is the end, how could it be otherwise. {idea}Look up. The sky above that grave was made without effort.{/idea} {reward}Bringing that person back is not harder.{/reward}
old: Bringing the dead back to life seems impossible.
new: If Allah made the heavens without tiring, raising the dead is well within His power.
try: Look at the night sky tonight and remind yourself that its Maker will raise every soul.

title: Is this not the truth? Yes, by our Lord.
subtitle: The confession that comes too late
then: On the Day the deniers face the Fire, they are asked if this is not the truth. Ibn Kathir says the question is: {trap}is this magic, or do you not see?{/trap} {idea}They have no choice but to confess.{/idea} The same word yes, said earlier, would have saved them.
now: You know deep down that something in your life needs to change. One day you will say yes, I knew it. {reward}The gift is saying that yes now, while it can still change things.{/reward}
old: I will admit it when I have to.
new: The yes everyone says in the end is worth far more if I say it now.
try: Admit one truth to yourself today that you already know but keep avoiding.

title: Be patient like the strongest Messengers; life is an hour.
subtitle: Closing comfort for the Prophet ﷺ
then: The surah came in the year of sorrow. Ibn Kathir names those of determination: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad ﷺ. He is told to be patient as they were, and not to hurry the punishment. {idea}On that Day, life will feel like an hour of a day.{/idea}
now: The hard season feels endless: the sick parent, the job search, the long exam year. {idea}Looking back from the Day, all of it will feel like one afternoon.{/idea} {reward}You are in good company in waiting.{/reward}
old: This hard stretch will never end.
new: From the end, this will feel like an hour, and the best of people were patient through theirs.
try: Name your current hard thing, then say: this is one hour, and I will be patient in it.
